title: JSON parse success is not lossless trace text serialization
applies_when: A trace or protocol exporter interpolates names, descriptions or dynamic object keys into JSON strings, or deletes quotes/control characters to make output parseable.
lesson: Validate both syntax and exact decoded content. A backslash sequence such as a literal Windows path can form valid JSON but decode into tabs/newlines; deleting quotes can silently rename markers. Use the format's encoder on each textual value/key and remove the surrounding hand-written quotes, rather than sanitizing or double-encoding. Exercise the actual database/file exporter and decompress/parse its output. Include ordinary and Unicode controls plus quotes, backslashes and control characters; assert names/descriptions are identical to the input, not merely that json.load succeeds. Check numeric fields and event envelopes separately so a text repair does not change their types. Follow producer types: a graph kernel count is numeric, not evidence that arbitrary text reaches that field. Search the original upstream implementation when working with a vendored converter before inventing a separate escaping routine.
avoid_when: Do not impose lossless text where the protocol explicitly requires normalization/redaction. Match the installed producer's source revision, including native submodules, against current upstream before proposing a new repair: an old wheel can reproduce an already-addressed defect. A SQLite fixture proves conversion of supported rows, not live device capture, current producer-schema compatibility or end-to-end performance. Direct component loading can isolate a stdlib exporter from an unavailable server package, but must be reported separately from installed-package/registered CI execution. This case is retrospective independent validation of a Scout lead, not a prospective selector comparison or a paper result.

evidence.note: Pinned SGLang converter interpolates operation text directly and removes quotes from API/marker/frame text. Counter and graph fields have different producer types; not every formatting placeholder establishes a user-controlled text defect.

Independent real-SQLite to gzip/JSON comparison: baseline has 8 JSON decoding errors, 2 silent corruption failures and 4 passing controls; repaired component passes all 14 subcases in 3 test methods on native Windows CPython 3.12/3.14. Registered package execution is blocked by resource import on Windows; no AMD capture/performance/merge claim.
The converter's original upstream already uses json.dumps for marker/API/operation text, supporting reuse of a standard encoder rather than a novel escaping algorithm or a whole upstream sync.
Kineto revision pinned by PyTorch commit70d99e9 (Torch2.11.0) sanitizes op_name without escaping quotes. This identifies the old producer mechanism, not current upstream behavior.

Current pinned source calls escapeQuotesForJSON after sanitizing event names. It still replaces backslashes with slashes; quote validity and lossless text are separate properties. Source-only comparison, not execution of a current wheel or proof of all trace fields.
